item.title: 'Is he crying?': Ajinkya Rahane & Murali Kartik slam India team selection as Mohammed Siraj appears emotional after being dropped for 2nd Test vs NZ
item.description: 'Is he crying?': Ajinkya Rahane & Murali Kartik slam India team selection as Mohammed Siraj appears emotional after being dropped for 2nd Test vs NZ originally appeared on Cricket News . Add Cricket News as a Preferred Source by clicking here . KEY TAKEAWAYS: Mohammed Siraj was missing again in Christchurch against New Zealand. Ajinkya Rahane & Murali Kartik hit out at what the television cameras showed. The selection call has raised fresh questions about India's long-term thinking. 'What's the point then?' Murali Kartik tears into India team management over repeated snubs to an emotional Mohammed Siraj in Christchurch Mohammed Siraj, once again left out of India's playing XI, looked visibly distraught and emotional on the opening morning of the second Test in Christchurch, and Ajinkya Rahane and Murali Kartik didn't hold back on live commentary. Since his Test debut at the Melbourne Cricket Ground (MCG) in 2020, Siraj has featured in every full away series India has played, but the team management decided not to pick him at Hagley Oval, ending that run. The decision has drawn plenty of attention because of the numbers behind it. The 32-year-old leads India's wicket-taking list in the ongoing World Test Championship (WTC) cycle with 43 scalps from 11 matches, which makes his omission harder for critics to understand. It also comes after a frustrating Test in Wellington, where India kept New Zealand under pressure for long stretches but couldn't bowl the hosts out in the second innings, and the game finished as a draw. Captain Shubman Gill won the toss and chose to bowl first on a surface with a green tinge. India made one change to the seam attack, dropping Prasidh Krishna and handing a maiden Test cap, number 321, to 26-year-old Punjab pacer Gurnoor Brar. Ravindra Jadeja was also left out again, along with Siraj. Murali Kartik on Siraj's heart-on-sleeve mindset after the India snub Rahane was the first to react when the cameras caught Siraj covering his eyes with shades to hide his emotions. "These visuals, is he crying?" Rahane asked. Kartik picked up the thread and drew on his own years in dressing rooms, where reactions to being dropped vary a lot from person to person. "I don't know, brother. He certainly looks quite emotional to me, because he is an emotional person," Kartik began. "Obviously, it hurts. Look, we have always played alongside all kinds of players; some are okay with it; there are some people who are fine when you drop them. "And then there are some people who just want to play; it doesn't matter to them if they have pain in their leg, pain in their head, pain in their body, or shivering, they'll give everything they've got. They put their life on the line. He seems like that kind of bowler." More to follow...

item.title: Yankees Shockingly Reportedly Among Teams Monitoring Randy Arozarena Market
item.description: Free agent outfielder Randy Arozarena The New York Yankees need help in the infield, but apparently that is not stopping them from keeping an eye on the outfield market. According to MLB insider Francys Romero , the Yankees are among the teams keeping an eye on Randy Arozarena. "Randy Arozarena continues to generate significant interest on the free-agent market, attracting multiple suitors as one of the top names available," wrote Romero on X on Nov. 18. "Teams such as the (Philadelphia) Phillies, Yankees, (Baltimore) Orioles, (Toronto) Blue Jays, (Houston) Astros, and (San Diego) Padres are among those monitoring his market." It does not sound like the Yankees are making a strong push to sign him, but they are at least keeping an eye on him. Arozarena is one of the best hitters available on the open market, and he would be a great addition for any offense. However, unlike the Padres, Phillies and Blue Jays, the Yankees don't have a hole in the outfield. It would be tough for the Yankees to find a place for Arozarena to play every day. The Yankees already have Cody Bellinger, Spencer Jones and Aaron Jude in the outfield. They cannot really rely on the designated hitter spot as long as Giancarlo Stanton is on the team. The Yankees should focus on finding a solution at third base to fix the offense before they resort to signing someone who does not have a clear fit in their lineup. The organization’s relative youth may help explain why. Thirty-three years sounds like a long time until you compare it with the histories of the NFL, NBA, MLB and NHL. Growing pains are to be expected, even with those leagues providing lessons to draw from. Besides, the UFC deals with unusually volatile personalities. These are people who try to hurt each other while wearing what amounts to underwear. That doesn’t excuse the UFC’s faults. There are plenty, and the promotion has made little or no effort to address some of them. But it seems fair to acknowledge what it does well. It’s the premier MMA organization for a reason, and most of us complaining have spent plenty of time watching its product. I hope nobody reading this watches the UFC solely to hate-watch. That sounds like a miserable way to spend a Saturday. Paramount+ makes watching the UFC simpler and potentially cheaper In the spirit of Thanksgiving, let’s consider what the UFC gives the MMA community. For starters, it consistently produces many of the sport’s most entertaining fights. That comes with trade-offs the promotion is frequently criticized for. A couple of decades ago, Fight of the Year candidates could come from almost anywhere. Pride Fighting Championships and HooknShoot delivered memorable bouts around the turn of the century. Strikeforce and Bellator MMA later provided plenty of competition. The Professional Fighters League and Rizin Fighting Federation still produce excellent fights, but the UFC now dominates much of the annual conversation. I think part of that comes from its reluctance to promote -- or sometimes even sign -- fighters whose styles don’t appeal to casual viewers. item.title: Five Levski fans taken to hospital as presidents condemn Marseille violence
item.description: Marseille police said 11 people were injured in the clashes, all of them Bulgarian (Justine MEDDAH) Five Levski Sofia supporters were taken to hospital after violence ahead of the Europa League game at Marseille on Thursday, with the French and Bulgarian presidents blaming the home fans. The lead-up to the match at the Stade Vélodrome was marred by confrontations in the stands between the two sets of fans, including the throwing of projectiles and flares. French President Emmanuel Macron condemned "in the strongest possible terms... acts of violence targeting Bulgarian fans", the Élysée Palace said. Bulgarian President Iliana Iotova said it was "unacceptable" and "shocking". "The attacks against the Bulgarian fans desecrate one of the great games that brings millions of people together around the world," she said in a statement on Facebook. "Everyone should be able to support their team without being afraid for their safety." Macron spoke to his Bulgarian counterpart on the sidelines of a European summit in Brussels, assuring her that "these acts would not go unpunished", the Élysée said. Several hundred Marseille fans ran from the stand where they were situated about 10 minutes before kick-off, appearing to pursue a group of Bulgarian supporters. They breached the stand designated for away fans, where around 500 Levski fans were gathered. Fighting broke out, with several Marseille fans wearing face coverings, an AFP journalist at the scene said. - 'Violent times' - "Five people were taken to hospital with eye injuries, head trauma and a dislocated shoulder," the Marseille police prefecture told AFP. "Six others were treated on site for various wounds." The police source said all the people injured were Bulgarian and there was "no information at this stage regarding any arrests". Iotova said: "The French authorities must clarify the circumstances surrounding the attacks and look for responsibility from those who committed them, and UEFA should check how the safety of the Bulgarian fans at the stadium was ensured. "We are ready to provide the necessary assistance to our compatriots. This behaviour is unacceptable!" Security personnel eventually managed to restore calm as the game kicked off on time. "It's a very regrettable episode -- these are incidents which are unacceptable for football," said Levski coach Julio Velazquez. "I support the fans who were caught up in this incident. I hope nothing serious has happened. I'm very saddened by this situation." Ligue 1 club Marseille said it was "working to understand the precise circumstances of these incidents". There were a few further flare-ups between the fans, notably during the half-time break. "We are living through violent times in our society, so this is very, very regrettable," said Marseille coach Bruno Génésio. The home team went on to win the game 1-0. stt/jc/nf/cms/pst

item.title: Eagles Security Forced to Step In as Nick Sirianni Appears to Confront Cowboys Fans After Historic Thanksgiving Win
item.description: Nick Sirianni ©IMAGO/Newscom World The Philadelphia Eagles seem to have finally caught a break this season. With a thrilling end to the Dallas Cowboys game on Thursday, head coach Nick Sirianni has plenty of reasons to celebrate. However, he might have gotten a bit too excited. As seen in the clips , doing rounds on social media, Sirianni is captured heading straight towards the Dallas fans with an agitated look after the win. Philadelphia’s chief security officer Domenico DiSandro, aka Big Dom, rushed to the scene to pull the head coach away from the crowd. Sirianni tried to charge back in. The heated rivalry between the two sides had the heat turned up with Sirianni celebrating the victory right in front of the home crowd. The Eagles head coach was so amped up after the win that he only gave a side hug to Dallas head coach Brian Schottenheimer, as part of the customary gesture after games. He didn’t even spare the losing coach a second glance and walked away right after. When a head coach's emotions boil over on the biggest stage, it reveals the intensity behind a dominant performance. Stay subscribed for the untold stories shaping the NFL's fiercest rivalries. What initially looked like a comfortable Cowboys victory turned into a stunning Eagles comeback, with Dallas surrendering a 31-10 lead before falling 39-38. Jake Elliott delivered the decisive blow with a 59-yard field goal with just two seconds remaining. The 21-point comeback was the largest ever in Thanksgiving game history for the NFL. The comeback was also made possible by an outstanding performance from Joe Milton, who delivered the best outing of his career. The Eagles quarterback threw for 331 yards and three touchdowns while adding a rushing score. In the fourth quarter alone, Philadelphia added 22 points. Dallas tried to stay in the fight with a crazy touchdown from Dak Prescott, who was briefly in the air but managed to hang on to the ball for the score. However, it was all in vain, as Brandon Aubrey missed a field goal later on. This is not the first time that Big Dom had to step up and calm Sirianni down. Back in 2024, the Eagles head coach got into a heated fight with Washington Commanders tight end Zach Ertz as they shook hands after the game. Even though the Eagles wrote one of the best comeback wins on Thanksgiving, the head coach’s reaction did not sit well with many. “Nick Sirianni is classless and should not be an NFL head coach,” Dr. Jeff Mueller wrote on X. “Buddy needs a nap and an ice cream sandwich to go chill out.” Walking back into the stadium after the game, that energy was still present in Sirianni. “We know how to fight,” he can be heard saying as he walks past the media. He also celebrated with Eagles fans nearby before he walked back in, high-fiving them. It all came about in a matter of minutes for Philadelphia, who were on a seven-game losing streak not long ago. Sirianni has reason to celebrate, but he sure will be asked about his behavior with the fans

item.title: Tom Brady rips into Aaron Rodgers for breaking ‘the sanctity of an NFL locker room’
item.description: Another Hall of Fame quarterback is coming out against Aaron Rodgers’ recent comments. This time it was Tom Brady, who kept it professional but made clear that Rodgers’ takedown of the Steelers after his benching needed to stay in house. “The sanctity of an NFL locker room, it’s a very sacred place,” Brady said on the Fox broadcast of the Eagles’ 39-38 win over the Cowboys on Thanksgiving in Dallas. “We shouldn’t ever lose track of that as players. It’s a privilege to be in that locker room. You’re fighting with your teammates, you’re fighting with your coaches, you’re always acting as a team together. Shouldn’t always be the place for private things to become public, that’s what I’ll say.” Fox Sports broadcast analyst Tom Brady looks on before the 49ers’ win over the Cowboys on Nov. 15, 2026, in Arlington, Texas. IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect The Steelers announced on Tuesday night that they were benching Rodgers against the Broncos in favor of Mason Rudolph, and Rodgers responded on Wednesday by going scorched earth on head coach Mike McCarthy during an appearance on “The Pat McAfee Show.” Among Rodgers’ gripes was the 19-year coach falling asleep in team meetings and leading a “1, 2, 3, Packers” chant after a huddle. The Steelers cut Rodgers soon after the appearance on “McAfee,” and he cleared waivers Thursday to become a free agent. Brady, who knows a thing or two about working with longtime coaches, acknowledged that feuds can happen in the locker room, but that doesn’t mean things need to boil over like they did in Pittsburgh. “I wasn’t a perfect player, [Bill Belichick] wasn’t a perfect coach, but we did some things in the game that we’re so proud of now,” Brady said. “And even me being four years removed from the game, things that matter more than winning a Super Bowl or trophy is my relationship with my teammates, my coaches. That’s going to transcend anything you do on the field. “It’s just unfortunate. I hate it, I hate to be even talking about it. It’s a privilege to be in the NFL. You want to inspire the next generation of athletes, and you always want to do it the right way.” Aaron Rodgers wears a frustrated expression during the Steelers’ loss to the Eagles on Nov. 22, 2026, in Philadelphia. IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect Brady wasn’t the only NFL legend who had something to say Thursday on Fox. Michael Strahan, Howie Long, and former Steelers quarterback Terry Bradshaw took time out of the pregame show to discuss Rodgers’ comments. While Rodgers now has the ability to sign with any team, his release by the Steelers may spell the end of his NFL career. ESPN insider Adam Schefter reported Thursday that it’s unlikely Rodgers finds a landing spot to finish out the season.

item.title: ‘This is unbelievable’: Stephen A. Smith shocked by what happened to the Cowboys against the Eagles
item.description: Photo by Tasos Katopodis/Getty Images for SiriusXM Stephen A. Smith always enjoys the Dallas Cowboys losing, but even he was shocked by their collapse against the Philadelphia Eagles. Thanksgiving games are always a joy to watch, and Cowboys fans would’ve felt really comfortable with the way their team played for large parts of the game. However, a late collapse saw them lose 39-38 to the Eagles, who pulled off the biggest comeback win on Thanksgiving in NFL history. Stephen A. Smith shocked by the Dallas Cowboys’ collapse against the Philadelphia Eagles The Dallas Cowboys looked to be in the driving seat to pick up a comfortable win against the Philadelphia Eagles on Thursday. The hosts dominated the first half and went in with a 28-10 lead at halftime. Midway through the fourth quarter, they were up 38-24 and could almost taste victory. However, the Eagles stayed alive via a blocked punt return TD, long touchdown bombs from Joe Milton to DeVonta Smith, and a game-winning push in the final minutes. Philadelphia pulled off a remarkable comeback to win 39-38 in the end, and Smith expressed his shock in the final moments of the game. He tweeted: “You can’t make this up! I can’t believe that the Dallas Cowboys are even in a position to lose this game. This is unbelievable!” Smith then posted a video of himself on X , laughing throughout and mocking the Cowboys after their disastrous collapse on Thursday night. The defeat is a massive blow for the Cowboys, who came into the game with a 5-6 record, and it just got worse. Their playoff hopes have been severely dented now. To add insult to injury, it was former Cowboy Milton who helped inflict the defeat, which must hurt even more. Up next for Dallas is a tough game against the Seattle Seahawks on the road. It remains to be seen how they will bounce back from such an embarrassing defeat. item.title: Jerry Jones hesitant to make major changes despite 'numbing' loss to Eagles
item.description: Jerry Jones hesitant to make major changes despite 'numbing' loss to Eagles originally appeared on The Sporting News . Add The Sporting News as a Preferred Source by clicking here . Jerry Jones is more accessible than most NFL owners, to the point that he reliably speaks with the media after each game. For Cowboys fans, that's a blessing and a curse; they get to hear an immediate response from the owner, but the words aren't always what they want to hear. After Dallas inexplicably blew a 21-point lead to the division-rival Eagles on Thursday, Jones was blunt about the shocking defeat but didn't offer much in the way of potential changes. Here's a look at what Jones had to say. MORE: Joe Milton likely secured NFL future with win over Cowboys Jerry Jones responds to Cowboys' collapse Jones called the loss to the Eagles "numbing" but said he "wouldn't anticipate" coaching changes despite the long layoff before the Cowboys' next game. "We can give ourselves a better chance to win these coming games and be competitive, in my mind, without coaching changes at this time," Jones said. That came with a caveat, though. Jones said "nothing we've seen out here tonight" gives him confidence in coach Brian Schottenheimer, but he added, "You've got to look at everything," noting that there are "several more games to go." Cowboys owner Jerry Jones says that “nothing we saw out there tonight” gives him confidence in Brian Schottenheimer, but he reiterates that a change is not on his mind right now. https://t.co/BipwLyTsE9 — Nick Harris (@NickHarrisFWST) November 27, 2026 As for the game itself, Jones was clear that everyone on the team, from himself to the players, shared responsibility. "It was ours to take, and we didn't," Jones said. "You have to question everything." QB Dak Prescott agreed with Jones' assessment of the loss. Told that Jones called the defeat "numbing," Prescott told reporters, "That's a good description for how I'm feeling right now." The Cowboys have yet to win back-to-back games this season, and they now trail the Giants by four games in the loss column. Jones typically resists coaching changes as long as possible, but the questions surrounding Schottenheimer aren't likely to fade anytime soon after a Thanksgiving collapse. Detroit Lions quarterback Jared Goff (16) throws a pass during the second half of the NFL game against the Chicago Bears at Ford Field in Detroit on Thanksgiving Day, Nov. 26, 2026. The Argentine claimed his 345th league victory last weekend to keep the Rojiblancos in the race to chase down Spain's traditional giants, Barcelona and Real Madrid. Third-placed Atletico visit Elche on Saturday with Simeone looking to keep adding to his record and deliver a third La Liga title, adding to his conquests in 2014 and 2021. Prying two league titles away from giants Real Madrid and Barcelona was an impressive achievement, and Atletico have shown this season they have the tools to do it again. item.title: Bayern risk more than sporting success as Musiala saga rolls on
item.description: Jamal Musiala signals to the bench with injury. (Alexandra BEIER) Bayern Munich head to Hamburg on Saturday in the middle of a crisis which threatens not only to derail the club's sporting ambitions, but their identity itself. Bayern, who are in the midst of an injury crisis which has decimated their forward line including Ballon d'Or winner Harry Kane, sit two points behind Borussia Dortmund in the Bundesliga table. But Bayern's treatment of midfielder Jamal Musiala by their hierarchy has led to a growing rift between the club and the playing group. Shortly after Bayern lost 2-1 to Lille on Wednesday, ending their run as the final unbeaten team in Europe's top-five leagues this season, vice-captain Joshua Kimmich suggested the club had fallen out of step with their values. "It's completely unacceptable and is not Bayern-like," Kimmich said on Wednesday, adding that Musiala's treatment was inconsistent with the club's "sense of togetherness". - 'Mia san mia' - This week, Bayern's hierarchy suggested Musiala take a pay cut as the 23-year-old battles his way back from a neurological condition which causes absence seizures. While the condemnation from media, player unions and former players was swift, Kimmich -- who was wearing the captain's armband with Manuel Neuer out injured -- was the first member of Bayern's current squad to speak out. Despite their status as one of football's perennial heavyweights, Bayern have always sought to emphasise their Bavarian roots and member-ownership in contrast to the American and Gulf-owned behemoths that loom over the European landscape. But their cold-hearted treatment of Musiala, a fan-favourite and popular inside the dressing room, threatens their carefully crafted identity. The club's vaunted 'Mia san mia' motto, which appears on every modern Bayern kit, translates to 'we are who we are'. Midfielder Aleksandar Pavlovic, a product of Bayern's youth system, in 2025 said: "For me, 'Mia san mia' means being a family, standing together in good times and bad. "That's what we live by here from a young age, that we always stick together." - Musiala's return - Just two months after signing a contract extension in February 2025, Musiala began treatment for symptoms of the neurological condition. After missing two months with an unrelated muscle injury, Musiala was warmly welcomed back by Bayern's 75,000-strong Allianz Arena on Friday. Minutes after full-time, club powerbroker Karl-Heinz Rummenigge suggested Musiala's condition meant he might be unable to deliver on his lucrative deal and should take a pay cut. "If he doesn't return to being the Jamal of old, then we need to have a conversation... because, frankly, the current financial figures would no longer be justifiable," he said. item.title: Verstappen spells out what truly puts him off racing in the Indy 500
item.description: Max Verstappen has revealed why he is unwilling to take part in the Indianapolis 500, citing the risks associated with oval racing and the serious accident suffered by Nelson Piquet at Indianapolis. The four-time Formula 1 world champion has made no secret of his ambitions to compete in other motorsport disciplines alongside his commitments with Red Bull Racing, with endurance racing among the Dutchman's main interests. However, despite his admiration for the Indianapolis 500, Verstappen is not particularly interested in testing himself at the prestigious American event. The Red Bull driver explained that his reluctance has nothing to do with doubts over his ability to be competitive, but rather with the risks involved. Verstappen cites Piquet's Indianapolis crash Speaking to the media ahead of the Qatar Grand Prix, Verstappen pointed to the accident suffered by three-time F1 world champion Piquet, the father of his partner Kelly, as one of the reasons behind his stance. The Brazilian suffered serious injuries to both legs and feet during practice for the 1992 Indianapolis 500, requiring extensive surgery and months of rehabilitation. Despite the severity of his injuries, Piquet returned to Indianapolis the following year and qualified for the race. Photo: Race Pictures Photo: Race Pictures Verstappen stressed that witnessing the long-term consequences of Piquet's accident has influenced his attitude towards competing in the American showpiece. "It's not that I think I won't be good at it. It's just the risk management. That's why I don't want to do it," Verstappen explained. "I like watching it, but I also know there is a very high risk involved by crashing, and I have had plenty of examples. "Even, of course, my father-in-law had a big crash there. And seeing how he had to live for the rest of his life after that crash is some risk that I'm not willing to take while already doing F1 and racing in GT3." The Dutchman also explained that, given the risks he already exposes himself to through his commitments in both Formula 1 and GT3 racing, he sees little reason to add another potentially dangerous undertaking to his schedule. "At one point, you're taking already a lot of risk. So sometimes then it's good to also have a few weekends where you don't need to be on the limit all the time."

Eighteen of 30 teams qualify for the postseason, meaning each one starts the season with a 60% chance of making the playoffs. No other major professional sports league in the U.S. is as generous. Yet the Galaxy failed to make the cut this year. And last year. In fact, the Galaxy have missed the playoffs four times in six years since Greg Vanney took over as manager. They also missed in three of the four seasons before Vanney arrived, meaning the Galaxy have cleared the lowest playoff bar in American sports just three times in the last decade. And they haven’t done it in consecutive seasons since Bruce Arena was the coach. Read more: Mauricio Pochettino's exit places U.S. men's soccer in a precarious state Arena left a decade ago. (To be fair, the last time the Galaxy did reach the playoffs, in 2024, Vanney guided them to a championship .) But wait, there’s more. Home attendance was down, dropping below the 20,000 per-game average for the first time in a non-COVID season since the Galaxy left the Rose Bowl for Carson in 2003. That’s a decrease of more than 18% since 2023. All this should be concerning for the team and its owners at AEG. The Galaxy, after all, used to be the model MLS franchise. It won the most games, had the best players, collected the most titles and led the league in attendance nine times. Today? Not so much. So does AEG have a plan to fix that? We reached out to Dan Beckerman , AEG’s president and chief executive, through a company spokesman, hoping for some clues. We never heard back. However, general manager Will Kuntz , speaking in a videoconference with the media Friday, agreed things are dismal. “I don’t think we did a good enough job collectively last year,” he said. “So for us, it’s really about taking a hard look at everything we’ve done process-wise and saying ‘hey, how can we be better?’ Because it cannot continue like this.” Galaxy coach Greg Vanney reacts during a match against LAFC at BMO Stadium on Oct. 25. (Luke Hales / Getty Images) Yet Kuntz, the architect of the MLS Cup team, may not be around to see that process through. Vanney still has two years left on his lucrative contract while Kuntz’s deal ends next month, so if there’s going to be a fall guy for the Galaxy’s recent failures, it’s likely to be the GM, not the coach. item.title: How Columbus Crew turned it all around to set up MLS playoff showdown vs. Messi
item.description: It wasn’t working. Issa Tall had to admit that. Well, he didn’t really have to. The results told the story for him. The Columbus Crew didn’t win in its first five MLS matches. By the World Cup break, 15 games in, they’d only added two more. There needed to be changes, and they needed to be big. The Crew general manager moved quickly. In May, he fired coach Henrik Rydström, his first coaching hire as the Crew’s chief soccer officer, though he was quick to point out he was involved with previous hires including bringing in Wilfried Nancy. He spent big in the summer, revamping the Crew’s attack and adding pieces while bidding farewell to some regulars. Ten players arrived, and eight went out. It worked. The Crew turned the boat around, going from worst in the Eastern Conference to closing the season on a six-game win streak and having won eight of their last nine. That was enough not only to jump out of Thursday’s wild card match but to set up a First Round playoff series with Inter Miami, the reigning champion led by Lionel Messi. They also pushed to the U.S. Open Cup final, falling to St. Louis City in a penalty shootout. All of it led Tall to believe he made the right decisions, moving on quickly from the coach he thought was the right man for the job. “Some people could’ve waited the full year. Maybe it would’ve been safer, but that’s not me. That’s not us as a club. That’s not even the way we play!” Tall told USA TODAY Sports ahead of the playoffs. “You see how we are bold and are not afraid of taking risk. At the end of the day, it wasn’t even a risk necessarily. It was necessary for our players, for our club as a whole and I think ultimately we made the right decision to do it at that time.” Tall still stands by Rydström as a good coach, something he’s proving while leading Hammarby in Sweden which currently sits atop of the table after running off five consecutive wins. But he wasn’t the right fit for the Crew in the post-Nancy era. item.title: Gotham FC’s title defense comes to crushing end in semifinal loss after venue change
item.description: They came by car, by the special-event X80 bus, by bike if they were feeling sporty. They came in layers, in beanies and scarves, with Gotham’s black-and-sky-blue colors on top. They came on behalf of those who couldn’t come, capacity being reduced at this impromptu change of venue, each one trying to make noise for five. Gotham FC forward Sam Kerr (20) competes for the ball against Kansas City Current defender Gabrielle Robinson (24) on Sunday, Nov. 15, 2026, in New York City. IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect They came with some measure of outrage — these home-field shenanigans would never happen in men’s sports — while their better angels told them to come in joy, in celebration, everyone watching women’s sports. And then, 25 miles and 20,000 seats removed from their regular destination at New Jersey’s Sports Illustrated Stadium, huddled in the bleachers by a blue track ringing an immaculate pitch at Icahn Stadium on Randall’s Island, in the shadow of the old Psychiatric Center and with the light fading over the Costco across the river, 5,000 devoted souls Sunday afternoon watched Gotham’s NWSL title defense end in a 2-1 semifinal loss to the Kansas City Current. “We lost today because we weren’t the better team,” Gotham winger and oracle Midge Purce said. “That being said, I would say it’s inexcusable. It’s not what you want in a professional league. It’s not what you want for women who are progressing in the United States and supposed to be one of the best leagues in the entire world. I think it’s a bad look for everyone involved. And we always want to be at Sports Illustrated in front of our fans when we earned that right throughout the season. But I would say it had no effect on performance today.” The match had been moved to Icahn on Monday due to concerns over the disintegrating field conditions at Sports Illustrated, which had unfortunately overshadowed Gotham’s quarterfinal victory there last weekend. Gotham was unbeaten in its past 13 matches at Sports Illustrated, which is operated by the Red Bulls of MLS. item.title: Beckham to be inducted into US Soccer Hall of Fame
item.description: David Beckham was knighted by King Charles in 2025 [Getty Images] David Beckham will be inducted into the United States' National Soccer Hall of Fame as part of its 2027 class. The former Manchester United and England midfielder, 51, made headlines in 2007 when he moved to Los Angeles from Spanish giants Real Madrid to join Major League Soccer (MLS) side LA Galaxy on a five-year contract. He made 124 appearances in all competitions for Galaxy, scoring 20 goals, and twice won both the MLS Cup and Supporters' Shield. Beckham's six seasons at Galaxy helped to raise the global profile of MLS and following his retirement in 2013, he became co-owner of MLS club Inter Miami, who signed Argentina World Cup winner Lionel Messi in 2023. His induction ceremony is set to take place on 16 April 2027 in Frisco, Texas. David Beckham's deal with LA Galaxy in 2007 was reportedly worth £128m [Getty Images] He was told the news he had been chosen on the veterans' ballot at an MLS board of governors' meeting on Thursday and said his time in the US has been "an incredible journey". Beckham, who had two loan spells with AC Milan in 2009 and 2010 while at Galaxy, added: "I'm looking to build this league and this sport in this great country for a long time." Meanwhile, former US internationals Megan Rapinoe and Julie Ertz have also been voted into the Hall of Fame in their first year of eligibility. Ballon d'Or winner Rapinoe, 41, and midfielder Ertz, 34, lifted the Women’s World Cup twice with with the US in 2015 and 2019. "To be alongside all the greatest players that have played for us, and played for our country alongside a bunch of my team-mates and friends, recognised like that in this way just means you were successful and a part of great teams," Rapinoe wrote on Instagram. item.description: Seattle Reign FC defender Phoebe McClernon, left, defends Gotham FC forward Guro Reiten during an NWSL playoff game in Harrison, N.J., Sunday, Nov. 8, 2026. item.title: Messi makes history with MLS Golden Boot
item.description: Messi retired from international football with Argentina earlier this year [Getty Images] Inter Miami forward Lionel Messi has become the first player in MLS history to win the Golden Boot in consecutive seasons. The eight-time Ballon d'Or winner scored 26 goals in 31 appearances, four clear of FC Dallas striker Peter Musa and five more than Nashville's English forward Sam Surridge. Messi becomes only the sixth player to land the award twice, joining a list that includes former Charlton Athletic and Southampton striker Bradley Wright-Phillips. In addition to his goals, the 39-year-old notched 17 assists over the course of the MLS season, ensuring his 43 goal contributions was also a league best for the second year in a row. And the World Cup winner could soon make more history as he bids to become the first three-time Landon Donovan MLS MVP winner. The former Argentina forward landed the award in 2024 as Inter Miami won the Supporters' Shield title and also in 2025 as they won the MLS Cup. Despite Messi's magic, Miami weren't able to land top spot in the MLS Eastern Conference, with the team finishing 17 points behind Surridge's Nashville. They will now face Columbus Crew over three games in the first round of the MLS Cup play-offs which begin later this month.
